stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria and null spec on a complex multi-surface live preview feature. Assigning both agents: openspec first to elaborate requirements and draft AC, then speckit to harden testability, security, and edge-case coverage.

agentContributions.notes: Story requests a new capability — Live Preview of CMS (Contentstack) content — that does not exist in the codebase. All content is fetched through useContent (236 callers), which is the integration point. ACs are empty; VCs derived from the description. Contentstack hosts are unreachable at test time, so criteria are written to our side of the boundary with mocked Contentstack responses.

Openspec produced empty acceptance criteria, so I built the full list from the story description, title, and file paths. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-5 establish the boundary — preview mode ON vs OFF — ensuring draft content is only served when a valid preview signal is present. (2) AC-2 defines the real-time update requirement with a 5-second SLA (adjustable based on Contentstack SDK capabilities). (3) AC-3/AC-4/AC-12 cover error and resilience paths: connection loss, malformed data, and initial fetch failure with fallback to published content. (4) AC-7 is a security criterion — preview mode must be gated so production end-users cannot access draft content. (5) AC-8 ensures all three brands (GO, UP, MX) are covered. (6) AC-9 ensures preview mode survives client-side navigation. (7) AC-10 ensures a11y parity between draft and published rendering. (8) AC-11 addresses partial-update granularity. (9) AC-13 covers the ContentstackLink component identified in the file list — referenced/linked content must also update in preview. CAVEAT: I could not read the actual source files (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx), so my criteria are based on file names and the story description alone. If useContent.ts has specific query patterns or contentstack.ts has specific SDK integration details, some ACs may need adjustment to match the actual architecture.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Brownfield ticket — empty acceptanceCriteria is expected per policy; judging verificationCriteria instead. All four declared manifest paths exist and resolved as exact matches across all three codelines (gotransit, upexpress, metrolinx) with zero unresolved paths. Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: OpenSpec identified useContent as the primary integration point (236 callers), established the test-time strategy of mocking Contentstack responses, and derived verification criteria from the story description. Speckit hardened the spec with security gating of preview mode (preventing production users from accessing drafts), error and resilience paths (connection loss, malformed data, fallback to published content), multi-brand coverage (GO/UP/MX), client-side navigation persistence, a11y parity, partial-update granularity, and ContentstackLink-specific criteria referencing the component in the file list. Verification criteria are observable: preview ON shows draft/unpublished content, preview OFF shows only published, updates appear in preview, production shows only published. The file set (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx) is plausible for a live-preview feature touching the content fetch hook, the CMS service layer, the content interface, and the link component. Speckit's caveat about not reading source files does not lower the score per policy.
